explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/405 (Erdős–Graham): for an odd prime p, does (p−1)! + a^{p−1} = p^k have only finitely many solutions? Yes (Brindza–Erdős). The Lean statement: the set of triples (a, k, p) ∈ ℕ³ with p prime, p odd and (p−1)! + a^{p−1} = p^k is finite. Finiteness is over all odd primes simultaneously, which is the meaning of the question and what was proved. Faithful.
